newsitem.title: USA: Smith & Wesson files complaint against Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Smith & Wesson files complaint against Brazil.

text.p: Firearms maker Smith & Wesson lodged a complaint with the U.S. government Thursday against Brazil, alleging discrimination against imported firearms.

"Smith & Wesson has invested substantial time and energy to sell our products to customers in Brazil, with little success, mainly due to trade barriers established by the Brazilian Government," the company said in a statement.
Springfield, Massachusetts-based Smith & Wesson is owned by Tomkins Ltd of England.
Smith & Wesson said Brazil had exported 2.5 million firearms to the United States since 1987 but U.S. makers combined have exported only 5,766 to Brazil.
It said an estimated 180,000 small firearms were purchased in Brazil last year, making that country the second largest market in the world for these products.
